arguments.command:
bash <<'SAVE_MAXIMAL_EOF' 2>&1 | tee "$HOME/save-maximal-$(date +%s).log"
set -u
OUT="$HOME/save-maximal-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
cd "$HOME/sovereign" || { echo "no ~/sovereign"; exit 1; }

echo "==== output: $OUT ===="
echo

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# [1] Pin the destroyed merge commit as refs/recovery/orphaned-merge
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== [1] Pin 6adf64b4d3 =="
git reflog --all --date=iso > "$OUT/reflog.txt"
if git cat-file -t 6adf64b4d3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  git update-ref refs/recovery/orphaned-merge 6adf64b4d3
  git log -1 --format='pinned: %H %ci %s' 6adf64b4d3
else
  echo "  6adf64b4d3 missing from object DB"
  echo "  searching reflog for the reset event..."
  grep -B2 -A2 'reset: moving to HEAD~1' "$OUT/reflog.txt" || echo "  (no reset event in reflog)"
fi
echo

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# [2] Pin every dropped stash found in unreachable
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== [2] Pin dropped stashes =="
git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs 2>/dev/null \
  | awk '/^unreachable commit/ {print $3}' > "$OUT/unreachable-commits.txt"
n=0
: > "$OUT/dropped-stashes.txt"
while read -r sha; do
  [ -z "$sha" ] && continue
  msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' "$sha" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$msg" in
    "WIP on "*|"On "*|"pre-merge"*|"autostash"*)
      n=$((n+1))
      git update-ref "refs/recovery/stash-$n-$sha" "$sha" 2>/dev/null
      printf '%s  %s\n' "$sha" "$msg" | tee -a "$OUT/dropped-stashes.txt"
      ;;
  esac
done < "$OUT/unreachable-commits.txt"
echo "  stashes pinned: $n"
echo

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# [3] Snapshot current HEAD/tree as a recovery ref (the "keep" side)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== [3] Snapshot current state =="
git update-ref refs/recovery/current-HEAD HEAD
git status --short > "$OUT/current-tree-dirty.txt"
echo "  HEAD pinned: $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
echo "  dirty files: $(wc -l < "$OUT/current-tree-dirty.txt")"
echo

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# [4] What did -X ours flip vs the destroyed 6adf64b4d3?
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== [4] -X ours flip report =="
if git show-ref --quiet refs/recovery/orphaned-merge; then
  git diff refs/recovery/orphaned-merge HEAD --stat > "$OUT/flip-stat.txt" 2>&1
  git diff refs/recovery/orphaned-merge HEAD       > "$OUT/flip-full.patch" 2>&1
  echo "  files affected by the flip:"
  cat "$OUT/flip-stat.txt"
  echo "  full patch lines: $(wc -l < "$OUT/flip-full.patch")"
else
  echo "  cannot diff — orphaned-merge not pinned"
fi
echo

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# [5] Side-by-side bashrc: current vs newest archive .bak
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== [5] .bashrc current vs newest .bak =="
NEWEST_BAK=$(ls -1t "$HOME/.dotfile-archive/.bashrc.bak-"* 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')
if [ -n "$NEWEST_BAK" ]; then
  cp "$HOME/.bashrc" "$OUT/bashrc.current"
  cp "$NEWEST_BAK"   "$OUT/bashrc.old"
  echo "  current:    $OUT/bashrc.current  ($(wc -l < "$OUT/bashrc.current") lines)"
  echo "  archive:    $OUT/bashrc.old      ($(wc -l < "$OUT/bashrc.old") lines)"
  echo "  unified diff saved:"
  diff -u "$OUT/bashrc.old" "$OUT/bashrc.current" > "$OUT/bashrc.diff" || true
  wc -l "$OUT/bashrc.diff"
else
  echo "  no .dotfile-archive/.bashrc.bak-* to compare against"
fi
echo

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# [6] Side-by-side claude/env: current vs newest .bak
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== [6] claude/env current vs newest .bak =="
NEWEST_ENV_BAK=$(ls -1t "$HOME/.config/claude/env.bak-"* 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')
if [ -n "$NEWEST_ENV_BAK" ]; then
  cp "$HOME/.config/claude/env" "$OUT/claude-env.current"
  cp "$NEWEST_ENV_BAK"          "$OUT/claude-env.old"
  diff -u "$OUT/claude-env.old" "$OUT/claude-env.current" > "$OUT/claude-env.diff" || true
  echo "  diff: $OUT/claude-env.diff"
  cat "$OUT/claude-env.diff"
else
  echo "  no claude/env .bak found"
fi
echo

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# [7] Every recovery ref we just made
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo "== [7] refs/recovery/* =="
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)  %(objectname:short)  %(subject)' refs/recovery/ \
  | tee "$OUT/recovery-refs.txt"
echo

echo "==== done ===="
echo "read these in order:"
echo "  1. $OUT/recovery-refs.txt         — every preserved ref"
echo "  2. $OUT/flip-stat.txt             — files -X ours flipped"
echo "  3. $OUT/flip-full.patch           — the flip, in full"
echo "  4. $OUT/dropped-stashes.txt       — recovered stashes"
echo "  5. $OUT/bashrc.diff               — your .bashrc decision"
echo "  6. $OUT/claude-env.diff           — your claude/env decision"
echo
echo "nothing changed in HEAD or your working tree."
echo "safe to rerun."
SAVE_MAXIMAL_EOF

  "$HOME/PROMPT.md"

for p in "${PATHS[@]}"; do
  if [ -L "$p" ]; then
    if [ -e "$p" ]; then

    else

    printf 'DIR          %s  (%s entries, mtime %s)\n' "$p" "$n" "$(stat -c %y "$p" 2>/dev/null | cut -d. -f1)"
  elif [ -f "$p" ]; then

echo "  count: $(wc -l < "$R/recent-files.txt")"
head -100 "$R/recent-files.txt"
echo "  (full list: $R/recent-files.txt)"
echo

# ============================================================
# 4. Dangling symlinks in relevant dirs
# ============================================================
echo "========== [4] Dangling symlinks =========="
for d in "$HOME/.config" "$HOME/.local/bin" "$HOME/.local/share" "$HOME/bin" "$HOME/sovereign"; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  find "$d" -maxdepth 4 -type l 2>/dev/null | while read -r l; do
    [ -e "$l" ] || printf '  DANGLING %s -> %s\n' "$l" "$(readlink "$l")"
  done
done
echo

# ============================================================
# 5. Every git repo under sovereign/projects (top-level only)
# ============================================================
echo "========== [5] Git repos (branch, HEAD, dirty count) =========="
find "$HOME/sovereign" "$HOME/projects" -maxdepth 5 -name .git -type d 2>/dev/null | while read -r g; do
  r=$(dirname "$g")
  br=$(git -C "$r" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null)
  hd=$(git -C "$r" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null)
  dt=$(git -C "$r" log -1 --format='%ci' 2>/dev/null | cut -d. -f1)
  d=$(git -C "$r" status --short 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  printf '  %-65s  %-22s  %-9s  dirty=%-4s  %s\n' "$r" "$br" "$hd" "$d" "$dt"
done
echo

# ============================================================
# 6. The rmtree'd state dirs — exist or gone?
# ============================================================
echo "========== [6] State dirs the scripts rmtree'd =========="
for p in \
  "$HOME/.agent" \
  "$HOME/.agent/tmp" \
  "$HOME/sovereign/tau/engine/checkpoint.json" \
  "$HOME/sovereign/tau/engine/.agent/tmp" \
  "$HOME/sovereign/tau/engine/.agent/checkpoint.json"
do
  if [ -e "$p" ]; then
    printf '  EXISTS   %s  (mtime %s)\n' "$p" "$(stat -c %y "$p" 2>/dev/null | cut -d. -f1)"
  else
    printf '  GONE     %s  <-- rmtree/unlink target, no backup taken\n' "$p"
  fi
done
echo

# ============================================================
# 7. Topology: sovereign vs projects (dir, symlink, or same inode)
# ============================================================
echo "========== [7] Topology: sovereign vs projects =========="
for p in "$HOME/sovereign" "$HOME/projects/sovereign-projects"; do
  if [ -L "$p" ]; then
    printf '  SYMLINK  %s -> %s\n' "$p" "$(readlink -f "$p")"
  elif [ -d "$p" ]; then
    printf '  DIR      %s  inode=%s\n' "$p" "$(stat -c %i "$p")"
  else
    printf '  MISSING  %s\n' "$p"
  fi
done
if [ -d "$HOME/sovereign" ] && [ -d "$HOME/projects/sovereign-projects" ]; then
  i1=$(stat -c %i "$HOME/sovereign")
  i2=$(stat -c %i "$HOME/projects/sovereign-projects")
  if [ "$i1" = "$i2" ]; then echo "  -> SAME INODE (duplicate mount, not a copy)"; else echo "  -> DIFFERENT inodes (two separate copies)"; fi
fi
echo

# ============================================================
# 8. Background processes that look like agent leftovers
# ============================================================
echo "========== [8] Suspicious running processes =========="
ps -eo pid,ppid,etimes,cmd 2>/dev/null | awk '
  /ralph|llama-swap|wezterm|opencode|nanocoder|openrouter|nim-proxy|flock|tau | omp |claude-wrapper/ && !/awk/ {
    print "  " $0
  }
' | head -40
echo

echo "========== done =========="
echo "report: $LOG"

What this reveals, section by section:

    Blast-radius paths — every file both scripts + the wezterm agent could have touched, with current state: FILE, DIR, SYMLINK_OK, BROKEN_LINK, or MISSING. MISSING on a path a script claims to write is the most important signal.

    .bak-* snapshots — the orchestrator's backup_file() helper makes a .bak-<timestamp> sibling before every overwrite. Anything with a .bak-* next to it can be reverted by cp file.bak-<ts> file.

    Recent changes in $HOME — the audit is time-anchored. Anything touched in the last week that you didn't expect is a candidate. This is the section most likely to surface something you forgot was touched.

    Dangling symlinks — this is where the wezterm cmdpicker or shell-integration symlinks would show up broken, and where the omp/tau/omp-tau-unified launcher chain would show up if the bash script was run and any target was moved.

    Git repos — branch, HEAD, dirty count, last-commit date for every repo under ~/sovereign and ~/projects. Cheap; run in one pass.

    The rmtree'd state dirs — GONE here means the Python script's shutil.rmtree on that path had no backup, and the content is only recoverable from filesystem snapshots or backups.

    Topology — whether ~/projects/sovereign-projects is a real directory or a symlink to ~/sovereign. Determines whether the duplicate-checkout logic applies at all.

    Processes — whether any of the daemons the scripts configure are actually running (in case they're holding state you're about to clobber).

import subprocess, os, json
from pathlib import Path

REPORT = Path(f"/tmp/sovereign-damage-{__import__('datetime').datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}.txt")
results = []

def run(cmd, cwd="/home/toxic/estate"):
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, cwd=cwd)
        return r.stdout.strip()
    except:
        return ""

# Find all repos
repos = set()
for base in ["/home/toxic/estate"]:
    for d in Path(base).rglob(".git"):
        repo = str(d.parent)
        repos.add(repo)
    for f in Path(base).rglob(".git"):
        if f.is_file():
            repo = str(f.parent)
            repos.add(repo)

print(f"Scanning {len(repos)} repos...", flush=True)
REPORT.write_text(f"SOVEREIGN DAMAGE SCAN - {__import__('datetime').datetime.now().isoformat()}\n{'='*60}\n\n")

damaged = []

for repo in sorted(repos):
    if not (Path(repo) / ".git").exists():
        continue
    
    # Check valid git
    head = run("git rev-parse --short HEAD", repo)
    branch = run("git branch --show-current", repo)
    if not head or head == "unknown":
        continue
    
    # Reset events
    reflog = run("git reflog --all", repo)
    resets = [l for l in reflog.split('\n') if 'reset:' in l.lower()]
    
    # Dropped stashes  
    fsck = run("git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs", repo)
    unreachable = [l.split()[2] for l in fsck.split('\n') if l.startswith('unreachable commit')]
    
    # Merge commits and their trees
    merges_raw = run("git log --merges --format='%H %P %s'", repo)
    
    repo_damage = []
    merge_pairs = {}
    
    for line in merges_raw.split('\n'):
        parts = line.strip().split()
        if len(parts) < 3:
            continue
        sha, parents, subject = parts[0], parts[1], ' '.join(parts[2:])
        tree = run(f"git rev-parse {sha}^tree", repo)
        key = parents
        if key in merge_pairs:
            if merge_pairs[key]['tree'] != tree:
                repo_damage.append(f"  PAIRED MERGES: {merge_pairs[key]['sha']} ({merge_pairs[key]['tree'][:12]}) vs {sha} ({tree[:12]})")
                repo_damage.append(f"    parents: {parents}")
                repo_damage.append(f"    {merge_pairs[key]['subject']}")
                repo_damage.append(f"    {subject}")
        else:
            merge_pairs[key] = {'sha': sha, 'tree': tree, 'subject': subject}
    
    is_damaged = len(repo_damage) > 0 or len(unreachable) > 0 or len(resets) > 0
    
    if is_damaged:
        damaged.append((repo, branch, head, len(resets), len(unreachable), repo_damage))
        status = "DAMAGED"
    else:
        status = "clean"
    
    print(f"  {status}: {repo.split('/')[-1][:40]:40s} | resets={len(resets)} stashes={len(unreachable)} merges_with_pairs={len(merge_pairs)}", flush=True)
    
    if repo_damage:
        REPORT.write_text(f"\nDAMAGED: {repo}\n")
        REPORT.write_text(f"  branch={branch} HEAD={head}\n")
        REPORT.write_text(f"  resets={len(resets)} dropped_stashes={len(unreachable)}\n")
        for d in repo_damage:
            REPORT.write_text(f"  {d}\n")
        REPORT.write_text("\n")

REPORT.write_text(f"\n{'='*60}\nSCAN COMPLETE\n")
REPORT.write_text(f"Total scanned: {len(repos)}, Damaged: {len(damaged)}\n\n")

REPORT.write_text("DAMAGED REPOS:\n")
for repo, br, hd, res, stash, damage in damaged:
    REPORT.write_text(f"  {repo} ({br}) HEAD={hd} resets={res} stashes={stash}\n")
    for d in damage:
        REPORT.write_text(f"    {d}\n")
    REPORT.write_text("\n")

REPORT.write_text(f"\nReport: {REPORT}\n")
print(f"\nDone. {len(damaged)} damaged repos found.", flush=True)
PYEOF

# Creating Claude Skills

Skills are reusable instruction sets that teach Claude how to perform specific tasks consistently and well. A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file and optional supporting resources. When triggered, Claude reads the SKILL.md and follows its instructions.

Think of a skill as programming Claude's behavior using precise natural language — where the LLM is the interpreter and the skill is the source code.

## When to Create a Skill

Create a skill when:
- A task needs **consistent, repeatable execution** across many conversations
- The task involves **specific tools, sequences, or output formats** that Claude wouldn't know by default
- You've iterated on a workflow manually and want to **capture what works**
- The instructions are too detailed to repeat every time but too important to leave to chance

Don't create a skill when:
- A simple prompt gets the job done
- The task is a one-off
- The behavior is already built into Claude

## Workflow

```
1. Capture Intent → 2. Research & Interview → 3. Draft SKILL.md →
4. Test with real prompts → 5. Refine → 6. Package & deliver
```

## 3a. Multi-repo damage scan (correct method)

Do NOT use bash loops that fork git per commit. Use Python + threads.

Discovery:
  fd -t d -H '^\.git$' ~/sovereign   →  repo dirs
  fd -t f -H '^\.git$' ~/sovereign   →  submodule pointer files
  (both — submodules have .git as a file, not a directory)

For each repo, in a ThreadPoolExecutor(16):
  - merge list:      git log --merges --format='%H %P'
  - reflog resets:   git reflog --all | grep 'reset: moving to'
  - dropped stashes: git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs
  - group merges by "parent1 parent2" key
  - any group with 2+ members: compare `git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}` for each
  - if trees differ → DAMAGED

Use git-snitch, git-scout, or gitgalaxy for the multi-repo scan if any of
them installed cleanly. Use them INSTEAD of hand-rolling, not in addition.

## 3b. For each damaged repo

Pin:
  git update-ref refs/recovery/merge-a-<sha> <merge1>
  git update-ref refs/recovery/merge-b-<sha> <merge2>
  git update-ref refs/recovery/pre-scan <current-HEAD>

Reasoned merge (per repo):
  - worktree at merge1^1
  - merge merge2^2 with --no-commit
  - for each conflict: read both sides' history, decide per file.
    Take A / take B / union / hand-write. No mechanical union. No side-picking.
  - for configs: merge keys, prefer newer unless older fixes a known bug
  - for code: merge functions independently, hand-write logic conflicts
  - for docs: merge sections, write the version that is true now
  - commit on the worktree, tag refs/recovery/maximal-merge

Use reconcile-ai OR gitwand-mcp OR pygitwise for conflict resolution where
they fit. Do not use `git merge-file --union` as the solution.

Write MERGE-DECISIONS.md at that repo's root. One entry per conflicted file:
  path:
  ours:   what our side changed and why
  theirs: what their side changed and why
  decision: take-a | take-b | union | hand-write
  reason: why that decision, referencing specific commits

## 3c. Cross-repo consistency

After all per-repo merges:
  - If the same file exists in multiple repos (herd.yaml in engines/herd/ and
    config/), decisions must agree. If they don't, one merge base is wrong.
    Find the true base and redo.
  - Submodule pointers in the parent repo must update to the merged submodule
    SHAs. Single commit at the parent listing old→new per submodule.
  - If a submodule was force-reset, the parent's recorded pointer may reference
    a destroyed commit. Fix the pointer only after the submodule's own merge
    is done. Never move a parent pointer to a SHA that doesn't exist in the
    submodule yet.

Three places you can put it, ranked by how well they match what it's for.

## 1. `~/.bashrc.env` — where your env vars already live

Your `.bashrc` line 2 is:
```bash
[ -f "$HOME/.bashrc.env" ] && . "$HOME/.bashrc.env"
```
So `.bashrc.env` is sourced **before** everything else in `.bashrc`. Put it there and it's set for the whole interactive shell, early, no ordering problem.

Append:
```bash
export OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"policies":{"privacy":{"region":"global"}}}'
```

**But**: `~/.bashrc.env` is a symlink into `~/sovereign/projects/shell/ii/dots/.bashrc.env`. Which means editing it:
- Modifies a tracked file in the `shell/ii` git repo
- The parent `~/sovereign` will see `shell/ii` as "modified content"
- The next `git submodule update --init` will revert it

If that's fine — commit it to the shell repo. If not, use option 2 or 3.

## 2. `~/.config/environment.d/99-opencode.conf` — modern, systemd-blessed

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/environment.d
cat > ~/.config/environment.d/99-opencode.conf <<'EOF'
OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT={"policies":{"privacy":{"region":"global"}}}
EOF
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user import-environment
```

Key facts:
- systemd's user manager reads `~/.config/environment.d/*.conf` on session startup
- Variables propagate to every process in the user session — shells, GUI apps, agents
- **Not sourced by bashrc** — different mechanism entirely, so no ordering concerns
- Takes effect on **next login**, not the current shell. To apply now:
  ```bash
  systemctl --user set-environment OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"policies":{"privacy":{"region":"global"}}}'
  ```
- Format is plain `KEY=value`, one per line. No quotes needed around the JSON if it has no spaces. The JSON has no spaces, so `KEY={"policies":...}` is fine as-is.
- **This is the correct place for this variable.** It's meant to apply to every opencode spawn, not just interactive shells. bashrc only affects shells.

## 3. `~/.bashrc.local` sourced at the end of `.bashrc` — if you must touch bashrc

If you want it only in interactive shells (unusual for this var, but possible):
```bash
# add to bottom of ~/.bashrc, AFTER everything else:
[ -f "$HOME/.bashrc.local" ] && . "$HOME/.bashrc.local"
```
Then `~/.bashrc.local`:
```bash
export OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"policies":{"privacy":{"region":"global"}}}'
```
`~/.bashrc.local` is not tracked by anything, so you can edit it freely. But this only helps interactive shells — background agents spawned by systemd, ralph, or your fleet coordinator won't see it.

---

**Pick option 2.** It's what the variable is designed for. It survives shell restarts, doesn't touch any git-tracked file, doesn't create ordering problems, and covers every opencode invocation — shells, subagents, containerized workers, everything in your user session.

Verify it took:
```bash
systemctl --user show-environment | grep OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT
# then open a NEW login (or restart the session), and:
pgrep -f opencode | while read p; do echo "=== $p ==="; tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$p/environ | grep '^OPENCODE_CONFIG'; done
```

That is a classic Hyprland double-bind bug: binding `SUPER + Return` and `SUPER + code:36` at the same time causes both to trigger on a single `SUPER + Return` press!

```
This is invalid WezTerm Lua! In WezTerm, setting leader key requires:
```lua
leader = { key = "a", mods = "CTRL", timeout_milliseconds = 1000 },
```
Notice two things:
1. The property in WezTerm config is `config.leader = ...` (or `leader = ...`), NOT `leader_key`.

MAXIMAL AUTONOMOUS EXECUTION PROTOCOL

You are executing autonomously. No check-ins. No "shall I". No summaries unless
a deliverable is complete. You create your own work.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BOOTSTRAP
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. Read your own state:
     ~/.agent/checkpoint.json
     ~/.agent/ralph-workflow.toml
     ~/.agent/tasks/*.json  (if any)
     ~/sovereign/MERGE-DECISIONS.md
     ~/sovereign/MERGE-DECISIONS-ROOT.md
     ~/tool-optimization.md
     ~/machine-diagnosis.md
     ~/repair-report.md
   If any of those exist, resume from where the checkpoint says you were.

2. If no checkpoint exists, create ~/.agent/checkpoint.json with:
     {
       "session_started": "<now>",
       "root_goal": "<the task you were given>",
       "task_graph": {},
       "completed": [],
       "in_progress": [],
       "blocked": [],
       "discovered": []
     }

3. From the root goal, generate a task graph. Not a linear list. A DAG.
   Each node:
     id           — stable, hash of description
     description  — one imperative sentence
     depends_on   — array of ids that must complete first
     deliverable  — what file or state exists when done
     verifier     — a command that returns 0 if the deliverable is valid
     estimate     — rough size (S/M/L/XL)
     method       — tool or approach
     status       — pending | running | done | blocked | failed
   Write the graph to checkpoint.json under "task_graph".

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TASK GENERATION RULES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Decompose every goal until each leaf task is:
  - Executable by one tool call or one small script
  - Verifiable by a shell command
  - Bounded in time (≤5 minutes)

If a task takes longer, it is not a leaf. Decompose it further.

When a task reveals new subtasks, add them to the graph immediately with
proper depends_on. Do not queue them mentally. Persist them.

When a task fails, do not just mark failed. Add a new task:
  "attempt alternate method for <failed task>"
with method = a DIFFERENT approach.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SCHEDULING
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Loop:
  1. Read checkpoint.json
  2. Compute ready set: tasks with all depends_on = done and status = pending
  3. Sort ready set by:
       a. Unblocks-the-most (fan-out)
       b. Blocker for user-visible deliverable
       c. Size (S first, they commit fast)
       d. Estimated value
  4. Pick top N where N = min(ready_count, max_parallel)
       max_parallel = 4 for CPU work, 8 for I/O bound, unlimited for subagents
       (ralph can spawn subagents)
  5. For each: mark running, spawn subagent or execute inline
  6. On completion: run verifier
       verifier==0 → status=done
       verifier!=0 → status=failed, append to discovered a retry with new method
  7. Persist checkpoint after every state change
  8. Repeat until ready set is empty AND in_progress is empty

If ready set is empty but pending tasks exist with unresolved depends_on,
inspect blocked tasks. Either:
  - Complete the missing dependency
  - Or the graph has a cycle: rewrite the graph

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PARALLELISM
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

For 1-off shell commands: run inline.
For anything over 30 seconds: spawn a subagent.
For scans over N items (N>20): Python with ThreadPoolExecutor(min(nproc*2, 32)).
For independent repos/files/subproblems: spawn subagents, one per shard.

Subagent contract:
  - input: task json (id, description, deliverable, verifier)
  - output: writes to ~/.agent/results/<task-id>.json
    { "status": "done|failed|blocked",
      "deliverable": "<path>",
      "evidence": "<command output or file hash>",
      "discovered": [ ... new subtasks ... ] }
  - never mutates shared state directly except its own output file

Parent aggregates results, updates task graph, schedules next wave.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TOOL SELECTION (mandatory, not advisory)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Filesystem scan:        ffs find / ffs grep      (NOT find / grep)
Code structure:         ast-grep scan            (NOT regex on code)
Semantic search:        tilth / semble / sia-code (when understanding code)
Multi-repo git audit:   git-snitch / git-scout   (NOT bash loops)
Conflict resolution:    reconcile-ai / pygitwise (NOT manual for >3 files)
Recovery:               gitundo / git-panic      (BEFORE any destructive op)
MCP search:             sourcegraph-mcp / hound-search-mcp
Long-running:           ralph / tau subagents
Env config:             ~/.config/environment.d/
Git safety:             refs/recovery/*         (never gc-able)

If a listed tool is missing, install it as a task before proceeding.
If install fails, note it and use the second-best tool. Do not block.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VERIFICATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Every task's verifier must be:
  - A command, not a description
  - Deterministic
  - Runs in <5s
  - Returns 0 only if the deliverable is genuinely correct

Examples:
  "test -f ~/tool-optimization.md && wc -l ~/tool-optimization.md"
  "git -C ~/sovereign show-ref --verify refs/recovery/maximal-merge"
  "rg '^<<<<<<<' ~/sovereign -l | wc -l"  (expects 0)
  "systemctl --user show-environment | grep OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT"

Do not accept "I did it" as verification. Run the command.

For aggregate deliverables (multi-file, multi-repo): verify every constituent.
A merge is not done until all its sub-repos are done and pointers align.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CONSTRAINTS (hard, non-negotiable)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

NEVER:
  - git reset --hard
  - git checkout -- .
  - git clean -fdx
  - rm -rf without archiving to ~/.recovery-archive/<ts>/ first
  - git stash drop
  - edit ~/.bashrc, ~/.bashrc.env
  - edit anything behind a symlink into a git repo without checking
    `readlink -f` first and committing if intentional
  - pipe to head/tail (use read tool with ranges)
  - claim success without running the verifier
  - stop mid-task because a single method failed
  - ask the user "should I..."

ALWAYS:
  - Pin recovery refs before any git operation
  - Check readlink -f before editing any file
  - Back up to .bak-<ts> before editing any file outside git
  - Persist state after every mutation
  - Report only at deliverables or true block

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
RECOVERY FROM FAILURE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Task fails → add retry node with different method, mark original failed
  Tool missing → add install node as prerequisite, retry
  Tool broken → add diagnose node, then retry
  3 consecutive failures on same task → mark blocked, add to blocked list,
    pick next ready task, return to it later with new method

Verifier fails → do NOT mark done. Loop the task.
  If 3 verifier failures → the task description is wrong. Rewrite it.

Graph has cycle → break it by splitting the offending task into two nodes
  with a data dependency instead of a control dependency.

Session ends (context limit, restart) → read checkpoint.json, resume.
  Do not start over. The checkpoint is authoritative.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
EXPANSION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

When a task reveals a problem outside the current root goal:
  - If it blocks the root goal: add it to the graph
  - If it doesn't block but is small (<5 min): add to discovered, do it
    opportunistically when the ready set is small
  - If it doesn't block and is large: add to discovered, do NOT do it now.
    Report it at the end.

When the root goal is done, do not stop. Read discovered. If discovered is
non-empty and within scope, promote the top-priority item to a new root goal
and continue. If discovered is empty, you are done.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
REPORTING
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Do NOT emit progress. Do NOT narrate.

Emit only when:
  a. A deliverable is complete AND verified
  b. A task is genuinely blocked and cannot be unblocked
  c. The full task graph is complete

Emit format:
  - what was requested (1 line)
  - what exists now (path + hash/verifier output)
  - what was NOT done and why (blocked list)
  - what was discovered but not done (discovered list)

No adjectives. No "successfully". No "I have". Just facts.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STOPPING CRITERIA
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

You are done when ALL of:
  - Every task in task_graph is status ∈ {done, blocked}
  - Every "done" task's verifier returned 0
  - discovered list has been triaged (done, deferred, or out of scope)
  - Final report emitted

You are NOT done when:
  - Ready set is empty but tasks are pending (graph needs fixing)
  - A verifier hasn't been run
  - A tool is missing and you haven't installed it
  - You feel tired (you don't get tired)

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

BEGIN.

Step 1: read checkpoint or create it.
Step 2: derive the task graph from the root goal.
Step 3: execute ready set.
Step 4: persist.
Step 5: loop until stopping criteria met.

/home/toxic/.claude/skills/smithers/llms-full.txt:`bunx smithers-orchestrator ui` discovers the workspace singleton, verifies that the answering process serves this workspace, and uses its advertised URL. When none is running it starts `smithers gateway` automatically (one per workspace: concurrent autostarts n on a lock and share the winner) and then opens the UI. `smithers gateway` serves workspace run state and workflow-owned `<UI>` declarations, with entry files resolved relative to the workflow that declared them. A workspace with no local `.smithers` pack and no prior run store still boots and serves the global pack alone. That is the headless sandbox shape: provision a VM with `bunx smithers-orchestrator init --global --yes --no-skill` (the default `bun install` inside `~/.smithers` is required for pack workflows to import) and `smithers gateway` serves the full pack, UIs included, from any bare cloned repo. Manage the daemon with `smithers gateway status` and `smithers gateway stop`. Use `bunx smithers-orchestrator ui RUN_ID --no-autostart` to fail fast when no Gateway is already running, or `--gateway <url>` for a remote Gateway. When the Gateway requires a bearer token, `ui`/`monitor`/`gui` route the browser through its session handoff so the printed URL opens cleanly; pass `--host 0.0.0.0` (or `SMITHERS_GATEWAY_HOST`) for Tailscale/LAN access, which auto-mints a token and prints dialable interface URLs.

content.text:
Unified code search/read tool. Replaces grep/glob/find/cat with token-budget aware output.

Usage: ffs [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  find        Find files by name (replaces `find` and `fd`)
  glob        Match files by glob pattern (replaces `glob` and shell `**`)
  grep        Search file contents (replaces `grep` and `rg`)
  multi-grep  Multi-pattern OR content search (Aho-Corasick; literal needles) [aliases: multigrep]
  read        Read a file with token-budget aware truncation (replaces `cat`)
  outline     Render a file's structural outline (functions, classes, …)
  symbol      Look up symbol definitions (NEW; tree-sitter AST powered)
  callers     List callers of a symbol (NEW)
  callees     List callees referenced inside a symbol body (NEW)
  refs        List definitions and usages of a symbol in one shot (NEW)
  flow        Drill-down envelope per definition (def + body + callees + callers)
  siblings    List sibling symbols (peers in the same parent scope)
  deps        Show a file's imports + the workspace files that depend on it
  impact      Rank files by how much they'd be affected if a symbol changed (NEW)
  index       Build / refresh the on-disk indexes (Bigram, Bloom, Symbol, Outline)
  map         Render the workspace as a tree annotated with file count and tokens
  overview    High-signal summary of the workspace (languages, top symbols, …)
  mcp         Run as MCP server over stdio (replaces agent built-ins Grep/Glob/Read)
  mention     Resolve a @-mention payload (Phase C surface — wraps the Phase B `resolve_mentions` engine API; tokens in the input become substring candidate queries against the repo)
  guide       Print the embedded agent guide
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --root <ROOT>                Root directory to search/index. Defaults to current working dir
      --format <FORMAT>            Output format [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
      --completions <COMPLETIONS>  Generate shell completions for the given shell [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]
  -h, --help                       Print help
  -V, --version                    Print version

# AI / LLM Proxy Router Definition

An **AI/LLM Proxy Router** (e.g. `paddock`, `sovereign-router-ts`, `9router`) is an API Gateway that sits between client AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, OpenCode, Cline, Copilot) and 40+ upstream LLM providers (NVIDIA NIM, Groq, OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Ollama).

## Core Capabilities
1. **API Interception & Multiplexing**: Accepts standard OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`) and Anthropic (`/v1/messages`) requests.
2. **Dynamic Provider Fallback & Load Balancing**: Automatically retries requests across fallback providers if an endpoint returns 429 (rate limit), 503 (overloaded), or fails authorization.
3. **Prompt Compression (RTK Token Saver)**: Strips redundant system context/whitespace to reduce token consumption by 20-40%.
4. **Token & Quota Accounting**: Tracks token usage, daily rate limits, and latency per provider node.
5. **Model Alias Mapping**: Maps abstract model names (e.g. `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `gemini-3.7-flash`, `qwen-2.5-72b`) to live healthy backend endpoints.

## What a Router is NOT
- **Not a Task Queue**: `flock` handles task queueing and distribution.
- **Not a Task / Oracle Engine**: `yote` handles task dispatching, bids, and oracle verification.
- **Not a Model Manager**: `herd` manages model binaries and weights on disk.
- **Not a Chat UI**: `squawk` handles human/agent chat messaging.
